newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate steady, baht down late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate steady, baht down late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate remained high at 13.00 percent late on Monday compared with 13.00-13.50 percent earlier and 12.75-13.00 late on Friday on tight liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers and a Bank of Thailand official said the recent buying of the dollar, the central bank's coming reserve requirement and some tax payments are the reasons behind the current tight liquidity.
All commercial banks have to meet the central bank's reserve requirement on the seventh and 22nd of every month.
"The money supply slightly improved in the afternoon after some major local banks were more willing to lend funds," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht edged down slightly to 25.494-25.498 to the dollar in late trade from 25.492-25.497 early on persistent demand for the dollar, dealers said.
"There remained strong bidding for the dollar today despite the high short-term baht intest rate," said one currency dealer. "It may be the dollar is still on a rising trend abroad."
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 9.20/9.70 satangs per dollar late from 8.50/9.50 in early morning.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.48 to the dollar against 25.47 on Friday.
